objective: Calculate unrounded areas by discriminant narrowing without modifying typed shape data.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Discriminated unions and branch narrowing are current TypeScript foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Selecting formulas from a tagged record is practical typed dispatch.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Trusted-input boundaries, immutability and floating results transfer to other numeric helpers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Three bounded variants keep the introductory union exercise focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A correct immediate result can conceal mutation of the caller’s dimensions.

defects: Typed shape domain, metadata preservation and unrounded formula behavior were implicit.
No test inspected the source after area returned.
A function that changed square.side after computing the right answer passed old checks.
rationale: Keep all correct boards and accept the equivalent if/else alternative. Define stable ordinary own/inherited data fields, optional freezing and bounded nonnegative fractional dimensions; formulas trust the typed input rather than validating unknown data. Three runtime assertions inspect frozen fractional formulas, actual mutable-source/metadata preservation and zero/fraction/boundary cases with a relative floating tolerance for equivalent circle evaluation orders. A readonly-object static call complements the existing wrong-discriminant-field rejection. Authored O(1) applies to the three fixed formula branches, not arbitrary JSON validation.

objective: Calculate full-precision perimeters with a never-typed exhaustive fallback and exact diagnostics.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Never and exhaustiveness checks remain current TypeScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: An explicit unreachable branch helps maintain tagged-record code.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Compile-time exhaustiveness versus runtime diagnostics transfers to other switches.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One formula helper builds directly on the previous union stage.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Premature rounding changes numeric results; an untyped fallback can hide a missing variant.

defects: The unrounded perimeter requirement was not tested at full circle precision.
Diagnostic behavior outside a typed valid shape needed a precise bounded demonstration domain.
A two-decimal perimeter implementation passed all old externally rounded examples.
rationale: Retain switch and exhaustive if/else boards. Explicitly keep full formula precision and the original exact Unexpected shape plus JSON.stringify diagnostic; it is not a runtime validator. Three runtime assertions inspect unrounded circles/fractional dimensions, diagnostics for undefined/null/primitive/array/record values and preserved input/metadata. A positive never-function/readonly-shape type assertion complements the original missing-rect exhaustiveness rejection. Earlier area tests remain cumulative. State O(1) only for valid perimeter formulas; serialization of an invalid diagnostic value has separate size-dependent cost.

objective: Parse the stated decimal grammar into a finite Number while preserving narrowing and null failure semantics.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Typeof narrowing and finite-number checks remain current TypeScript basics.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Strict bounded decimal input conversion is practical form/data work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Grammar versus conversion overflow and exact trim behavior transfer to other parsers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One precise decimal grammar keeps the introductory parser bounded.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A syntactically valid decimal can become Infinity and escape a finite-result contract.

defects: All three boards returned nonfinite overflow for long matching decimal strings.
String length/trim/ASCII grammar, underflow/signed zero and precision boundaries were implicit.
The original hint and explanation omitted the post-conversion finite check.
rationale: Check Number.isFinite after string conversion on every board, and add a visible overflow example plus matching prompt/hint/explanation guidance. Retain finite primitive numbers unchanged; preserve signed zero/ordinary Number precision and reject prefix parsing, plus signs, exponents, hex, missing integer/fraction digits and non-ASCII digits. Three hidden assertions cover overflow, JavaScript whitespace versus zero-width text, signed zero,1000-unit strings/underflow and rejected grammar. A boolean-argument static negative complements existing nullable-result typing. An independent character-scan alternative validates the same grammar and conversion. Its initial unknown[] reduce accumulator in a later alternative was explicitly typed before baseline acceptance; raw initial evidence remains separate. Final wording rereading prompted a six-case stage-three recheck after the hint/explanation update. Target O(n) in string length.

objective: Narrow unknown stable data by an actual nonmutating boolean shape guard with finite nonnegative dimensions.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Unknown boundaries and user-defined predicates remain current TypeScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Checking a tagged record before using a formula is practical validation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Exact property domains, no coercion and nonmutating guards transfer to adapters.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One discriminant and at most two fields keep this guard bounded.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A predicate that sanitizes dimensions can silently alter data while returning the expected boolean.

defects: Own/inherited fields, decorated arrays/boxed objects and unrelated metadata were unspecified.
No test inspected dimensions after a true predicate result.
A guard that zeroed accepted sizes passed every original boolean-only example.
rationale: Retain all three sound nonmutating guards; do not arbitrarily add an own/plain-object restriction to the original non-null-object contract. Define stable data without accessors/proxies, accepted decorated arrays/boxed objects and inherited data, exclusion of functions/primitives, no numeric coercion, and all finite nonnegative dimensions including large finite values. Three runtime assertions cover those objects, missing/invalid/nonfinite/negative fields, actual boolean outputs and mutable/frozen source preservation. A positive predicate-signature/narrowing case complements old unsafe-unknown rejection. Carry finite decimal parsing and earlier area/perimeter tests forward. O(1) checks only fixed fields; formula inputs retain their separately bounded domain.

objective: Sum accepted shape occurrences without mutation and round the accumulated full-precision total once.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Readonly unknown arrays, guards and typed aggregates remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Validating and aggregating mixed records is practical data work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Rounding stage, duplicate occurrences and fresh result ownership transfer to numeric summaries.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A bounded array combines the four earlier narrowing helpers.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Rounding each item or mutating accepted records produces incorrect totals or later behavior.

defects: The input signature unnecessarily required a mutable array.
No case distinguished final-total rounding from per-item rounding.
Fresh exact result ownership, repeated identities, inherited/decorated shape data and bounds were untested.
rationale: Widen all boards to readonly unknown[] while preserving existing one-pass and filter/reduce implementations. Define dense stable bounded arrays and accepted dimensions within the formula-stage bound; count every occurrence, including repeated references and zero-area shapes. Three runtime assertions distinguish four small-circle final rounding from per-area rounding, inspect fresh exact mutable result fields and preserved inherited/decorated inputs, and exercise1000 entries. Add readonly input/mutable result static acceptance; retain wrong-result type rejection. The independent one-pass reduce alternative uses an explicit accumulator type so unknown[] does not infer unknown. Fifteen distinct hidden and one visible runtime assertion execute48 times cumulatively; five new static assertions execute15 times across stages. Target O(n) with bounded fixed-field formulas and permit the valid senior O(n)-auxiliary-space implementation.
